claims.text: In Q235 steel, pre-exposure microstructure influences the formation of protective Fe-oxide scales during thermal annealing.
Annealing Q235 steel in air at 700 °C can produce a fine-grained, continuous oxide scale along grain boundaries.
A fine-grained, continuous Fe-oxide scale limits oxygen and salt diffusion.
Limiting oxygen and salt diffusion preserves hardness and reduces mass change during high-temperature and room-temperature salt exposure.
Over-annealing promotes grain growth and discontinuities in the oxide scale.
Grain growth and oxide-scale discontinuities increase localized corrosion.
Annealing Q235 steel in air at 700 °C for 0.5, 1, and 2 hours will develop distinguishable oxide-scale microstructures.
The relevant structural mediator is the formation, adhesion, continuity, grain size, and grain distribution of Fe-oxide scales.
The pre-exposure microstructure of Q235 steel determines the diffusion paths available during oxidation.
A fine-grained structure supports formation of a continuous and adherent oxide scale.
A continuous, adherent oxide scale can self-heal during cyclic thermal and salt exposure.
Over-annealed samples with enlarged grains develop scale discontinuities and voids that permit penetration by aggressive salts.
Relative to un-annealed Q235 steel, samples having fine-grained, continuous oxide scales will show lower mass change under the specified salt exposures.
Relative to un-annealed Q235 steel, samples having fine-grained, continuous oxide scales will retain more hardness.
Relative to un-annealed Q235 steel, samples having fine-grained, continuous oxide scales will show fewer signs of microstructural degradation and localized corrosion.
Over-annealed samples with coarse oxide scales will show more localized corrosion and degradation than samples with fine-grained, continuous scales.
The proposed mechanism is limited to oxidation in air at 700 °C followed by exposure to the defined Na2SO4-NaCl salt regimes at room temperature or 700–900 °C.
The mechanism may not apply under reducing atmospheres, substantially different temperatures, or significantly different salt compositions.
The optimal annealing duration may vary with subtle composition or processing variations in Q235 steel.
